A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the fatty-acyl composition of retinol esters in the liver of pinnipeds is highly variable and that the pool of acyldonors used to esterify retinol is different from that used to synthesize other liver lipids.
the fatty-acyl composition of retinol esters in marine-mammal liver is not determined solely by the acyl composition of whole-liver lipoprotein, as has been assumed.

the fatty-acid composition and concentration of vitamin A in the livers and retinyl ester of pinnipeds are different from those of most other mammals and birds.
the pool of acyldonors used for esterifying retinol may differ from that used for the esterifcation of other lipids.
